title: Road Markings Across the Road & at the Kerb
whatItIs: Lines across the road show where to stop or give way; yellow lines and kerb marks show where you cannot wait or load.

keyFacts.text: A double broken white line across your lane means you MUST give way to traffic on the major road.
At a STOP sign you MUST stop behind the solid white line.
You MUST NOT enter a box junction until your exit road or lane is clear.

keyFacts: Double yellow lines: no waiting at any time. Single yellow: no waiting at the times shown on nearby plates.
Yellow marks on the kerb restrict loading: one mark at the times shown, two marks at any time.

visual.caption: Lines across the road and at the edge

items.label: Give way line
items.meaning: Give way to traffic on the road you're joining.

items.label: Stop line
items.meaning: Used with a STOP sign: you MUST stop behind it.

items.label: Box junction
items.meaning: Don't enter until your exit is clear.

items.label: Single yellow line
items.meaning: No waiting at the times shown on the plate.

items.label: Two yellow kerb marks
items.meaning: No loading or unloading at any time.

a.label: Yellow lines on the road
points: Single: times shown. Double: any time

b.label: Yellow marks on the kerb
points: One mark: times shown. Two: any time

onTheTest.question: When may you wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: When your exit is blocked by queuing traffic
When turning right and only oncoming traffic stops you
Whenever the traffic lights are red
onTheTest.why: You must not enter until your exit is clear, but you may wait in the box when turning right if only oncoming traffic or other right-turners are holding you up.

traps: Kerb marks control loading; yellow lines control waiting.
A give way line doesn't always mean stop: stop only if you need to.
'Never' is wrong for box junctions: turning right is the exception.
